about: Tekken-style systems added to Street Fighter 6, offline only. One row per system. 'n/a' means the column does not apply to that row. Every cell must be filled. Heat follows Tekken 8: once per round, a 10 second timer that stops while the opponent is hit, no general damage bonus, and chip damage on block that cannot KO and that you win back by landing attacks. chip_pct_of_max and recover_pct_of_max_per_landed_attack are my estimates: Tekken's chip is 20% of the blocked attack's damage, which SF6 does not give us on a block yet. Rage follows Tekken 8 (season 3): active at 45 of 180 health (25%), +10% damage rounded down, and 70% less chip damage taken. A hit on a fighter who is not in Heat removes 30% of its damage from their recoverable health (from the Wavu wiki summary; whether the victim must be standing is not checked here). Heat Smash and Rage Art are stand-ins: they are damage bonuses on your next landed hit, armed with a key, not real moves. bonus_pct_of_max, armed_ticks and heat_start_heals_pct_of_pool are my estimates for fun, not Tekken's numbers. slowmo_fx slows the whole game for fx_frames screen frames at fx_speed_scale (1.0 = normal) when a Heat Smash or Rage Art lands. It is an experiment: it is off until the user tests it, and it turns itself off if the game refuses it. fx_method names which hook slows the game: global_speed, scene_time_scale or max_fps.

rows.note: Tekken 8 Rage: at or under 25% health (45 of 180), every hit deals 10% more damage (rounded down) and chip damage taken is cut by 70%. Not possible here: Rage Art. The earlier numbers (20%, +15%) were verified working in game; these new numbers are untested. User played the Tekken 8 version offline and reported 'it feels good now' (2026-10-07). That is a general confirmation: the individual readouts were not reviewed one by one.

Tekken 8 Heat: press the key (P1 F1 = 112, P2 F2 = 113) to start Heat. It can be used once per round and lasts 10 seconds of running time (600 match ticks, about 60 per second); the timer stops while the opponent is in hitstun. Heat gives no damage bonus. A blocked hit costs the blocker chip damage that cannot KO; it is recoverable and is won back when the chipped fighter lands attacks. Not possible here: Heat Smash, Heat Dash, Heat Burst (2+3) input and Engager moves. Earlier version (+15% damage, 20 second cooldown, permanent chip) was verified in game; this version is a redesign and is untested. User played the Tekken 8 version offline and reported 'it feels good now' (2026-10-07). That is a general confirmation: the individual readouts were not reviewed one by one.
Tekken-style longer juggles by easing SF6's combo damage scaling. Not built: first find out what the probe says about combo_dm_air, and which data controls scaling.

Heat Smash stand-in: press the Heat key again while Heat is running to arm it for 2 seconds. The next hit that lands deals extra damage (15% of max health) and uses up your remaining Heat. If it does not land in time, the Heat is spent anyway. A blocked attack does not use it up. Not the real move: no animation, no armor. User played the Tekken 8 version offline and reported 'it feels good now' (2026-10-07). That is a general confirmation: the individual readouts were not reviewed one by one.

Rage Art stand-in: while in Rage, press the key (P1 F3 = 114, P2 F4 = 115) to arm it for 2 seconds, once per round. The next hit that lands deals extra damage (18% of max health), removes the opponent's recoverable health, wins back some of yours, and ends your Rage. If it does not land in time, Rage still ends. Not the real move: no animation or cinematic. User played the Tekken 8 version offline and reported 'it feels good now' (2026-10-07). That is a general confirmation: the individual readouts were not reviewed one by one.

Experimental impact slow-motion: when a Heat Smash or Rage Art lands, slow the game to 35% for about 0.75 seconds. Off by default; try the test button in the panel first, then tick the box. It turns itself off if the game refuses the call. Test 2026-10-07: the global speed method did not visibly slow the game, so two other methods (scene time scale, lower frame cap) can be selected in the panel and tried.
Weightier hits: first find out which field is the game's hit freeze and whether it can be written. The panel shows the live values of all three candidates.
